Zero-inflated negative binomial regression by EM with IRLS M-steps

Source: R/zinbreg.R
zinbreg.Rd

Fits the ZINB model: with probability pi an observation is a structural zero, and otherwise it follows an NB2 distribution with mean mu, where log(mu) = X beta + offset and logit(pi) = Z gamma. The observed-data log-likelihood is maximized by the EM algorithm. The E-step computes the posterior probability that each zero is structural; the M-step fits a logistic regression with that fractional response (by IRLS) and a weighted NB regression (IRLS for beta, Newton-Raphson for theta). No general-purpose optimizer is used. Standard errors come from the analytic observed information matrix of (beta, gamma, log(theta)). The results reproduce pscl::zeroinfl(..., dist = "negbin").

Usage

zinbreg(
  formula,
  data,
  offset,
  control = zinbreg_control(),
  weights,
  subset,
  na.action
)

Arguments

formula

A two-part formula y ~ x1 + x2 | z1 + z2: count-model covariates before |, zero-model covariates after it. Without |, the same covariates are used in both parts.

data

A data frame containing the variables in formula.

offset

Optional offset for the count model, evaluated in data. Offsets can also be given with offset() in either part of the formula.

control

A list from zinbreg_control().

weights

Optional non-negative prior weights.

subset

Optional expression selecting the rows of data to use.

na.action

How to handle missing values.

Value

An object of class "zinbreg": a list containing coefficients (a list with elements count and zero), vcov (covariance matrix of all coefficients and log(theta)), theta, SE.theta, SE.logtheta, loglik, iter, converged, fitted.values ((1 - pi) mu), mu, pi, call, and the model information needed by predict.zinbreg().

See also

zinbreg-methods, nbreg()

Examples

data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")
fit <- zinbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment | ment,
               data = bioChemists)
summary(fit)
#> 
#> Call:
#> zinbreg(formula = art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment | ment, 
#>     data = bioChemists)
